earth.title: TerraTwin earth integrated dataset

grid.cell_id: row * n_lon + col, row 0 = northernmost, col 0 = -180 E

sources.name: NOAA ETOPO 2022 15 arc-second global relief model (ice surface) + Natural Earth 1:10M land and lake masks
sources.provider: NOAA NCEI (ETOPO 2022); Natural Earth (land polygons)
sources.citation: NOAA NCEI (2022) ETOPO 2022 15 Arc-Second Global Relief Model, doi:10.25921/fd45-gt74; Natural Earth 1:10m land v5.
sources.limitations: Land mask is 1:10M scale (coastline ~1 km accurate), so coastal cells mix a few sea pixels; large lakes are masked because ETOPO maps their floor (e.g. Baikal), not the water surface.

sources.name: Confirmed terrestrial impact structures (Wikipedia list compiled from the Earth Impact Database), pinned revision
sources.provider: Wikipedia (List of impact structures on Earth, revision 1381890264, 2026-10-25); primary data PASSC Earth Impact Database (UNB)
sources.citation: Earth Impact Database (2026) Planetary and Space Science Centre, UNB; Wikipedia contributors, List of impact structures on Earth (CC BY-SA 4.0).
sources.limitations: Earth keeps very few craters (erosion, plate tectonics, vegetation), so densities are near zero almost everywhere and are not comparable 1:1 with Moon/Mars surface ages; the official EID site (passc.net) was offline, so the Wikipedia transcription is used; coordinates missing from the list are taken from the Wikidata item of the linked article (rows whose link resolves to no item with coordinates are dropped); size-frequency slope cannot be fitted (never >=10 craters in a window) and is omitted.

sources.name: Global lithology class at 250 m from the USGS Global Ecosystem Map (EcoTapestry), OpenLandMap
sources.provider: OpenLandMap (T. Hengl) from USGS Global Ecosystems (Sayre et al. 2014)
sources.citation: Hengl T. (2018) doi:10.5281/zenodo.1464846; Sayre R. et al. (2014) A New Map of Global Ecological Land Units, AAG.
sources.limitations: Lithology only (no chronostratigraphic age, so geo_age is absent for Earth); generalized from the Global Lithological Map (GLiM, ~1:3.75M); no Antarctica.

sources.name: Long-term MODIS (MOD11A2) land surface temperature, monthly day/night median 2000-2017, 1 km (OpenLandMap)
sources.provider: OpenLandMap (T. Hengl) from NASA LP DAAC MOD11A2 v006
sources.citation: Hengl T. (2018) doi:10.5281/zenodo.1420115; Wan Z. et al. (2015) MOD11A2 v006, NASA LP DAAC.
sources.limitations: Terra overpass times (~10:30 / ~22:30) sample the diurnal cycle twice, so max/min are below the true afternoon peak and pre-dawn minimum; clear-sky only (cloudy regions biased warm at night / cool by day); no Antarctica.

sources.name: ERA5 reanalysis monthly means 2001-2020 (surface pressure, wind, stress, solar flux, snow, albedo, soil water)
sources.provider: ECMWF / Copernicus C3S, distributed by NCAR GDEX dataset d633001 via OSDF (anonymous)
sources.citation: Hersbach H. et al. (2020) QJRMS 146, 1999-2049; ECMWF (2019) ERA5 Reanalysis Monthly Means, NCAR GDEX doi:10.5065/P8GT-0R61.
sources.limitations: Reanalysis (model constrained by observations), coarser than the 0.125 deg grid (cells inherit the containing 0.25 deg value); snow depth is capped at 10 m w.e. over glaciers; stress magnitude is taken from monthly-mean components (underestimates gusty stress).

sources.name: Global map of wind-blown sand dune presence (dune-world, Nature Communications 2026)
sources.provider: geomorphlab / A. Gunn et al. (GitHub dune-world, rev1)
sources.citation: The distribution of Earth's wind-blown sand dunes (2026) Nature Communications, doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75466-y; code/data doi:10.5281/zenodo.20054674.
sources.limitations: 0.1 deg presence mask (not dune-field polygons as for Mars MGD3); cover fraction is the share of 0.1 deg dune pixels centred in the cell.

sources.name: Natural caves with coordinates from Wikidata (lava tubes flagged)
sources.provider: Wikidata Query Service (CC0)
sources.citation: Wikidata contributors, Wikidata (CC0), query of instances of cave (Q35509) on Earth.
sources.limitations: Crowd-sourced and incomplete (~15k caves, only ~50 lava tubes); mostly karst caves, unlike lunar/martian pits; no depth/diameter, so nearest_cave_depth_diam_ratio is absent for Earth.

sources.name: Analytic orbital-geometry model (top-of-atmosphere insolation)
sources.provider: TerraTwin derivation from standard celestial mechanics
sources.citation: Standard insolation formula (e.g., Berger 1978); Earth e=0.0167, obliquity 23.44 deg.
sources.limitations: Top-of-atmosphere only; ERA5 insolation_surface_wm2 includes cloud and aerosol attenuation.

limitations: Land cells only (any land pixel in the 0.125 deg cell); oceans are excluded because Earth analogs are land surfaces.
No Earth equivalent of orbital gamma-ray/neutron geochemistry (FeO, SiO2, K, Th, neutron counts) exists globally; those Moon/Mars features are absent, not zero.
MODIS LST and the lithology map do not cover Antarctica (south of 62 S): temperature and geology are NaN there.
MODIS samples ~10:30 and ~22:30 local time only, so tsurf_max_k / tsurf_min_k understate the true diurnal extremes.
Pressure, wind, stress, surface insolation, snow, albedo and soil water are ERA5 reanalysis (model), 0.25 deg.
Craters: ~190 confirmed structures; densities are near zero almost everywhere and say little about surface age on Earth.
Caves are a crowd-sourced Wikidata catalog (mostly karst, ~50 lava tubes), heavily biased to well-documented countries.
No global rock-abundance, thermal-inertia, dust-opacity or gravity grid was available without registration; those features are absent for Earth.
Earth hosts life everywhere; Moon/Mars habitability proxies (biosignature preservation) are not computed for Earth.

moon.title: TerraTwin moon integrated dataset

grid.cell_id: row * n_lon + col, row 0 = northernmost, col 0 = -180 E

sources.name: LRO LOLA Gridded DEM, 64 pixels/degree (LDEM_64)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (LRO LOLA team, GSFC)
sources.citation: Smith D.E. et al. (2010) GRL 37, L18204; Neumann G.A. (2010) LRO-L-LOLA-4-GDR-V1.0, NASA PDS.
sources.limitations: Interpolated between LOLA tracks at low latitudes (track gaps up to ~1-2 km); slopes below ~1 km baseline are not resolved.

sources.name: Diviner Global Cumulative Product - binned brightness/bolometric temperatures by local time
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Diviner team, UCLA)
sources.citation: Williams J.-P. et al. (2017) Icarus 283, 300-325.
sources.limitations: Binned average of nadir observations; -9999 = no observation; 0.5 deg bins cannot resolve km-scale cold traps.

sources.name: Diviner Polar Resource Product (annual temperatures and ice-stability depth)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Diviner team, UCLA)
sources.citation: Paige D.A. et al. (2010) Science 330, 479; Siegler M.A. et al. (2016) Nature 531, 480.
sources.limitations: temp_avg/ice_depth come from a thermal model constrained by Diviner, not direct observation of ice.

sources.name: Diviner rock abundance and regolith (soil) temperature, 32 ppd
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Diviner team)
sources.citation: Bandfield J.L. et al. (2011) JGR 116, E00H02.
sources.limitations: Retrieval assumes two-component (rock + regolith) surface; rocks are >~1 m; poleward of 60 deg not provided.

sources.name: Lunar Prospector GRS elemental abundances (2 deg equal-area)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Prettyman et al.)
sources.native_resolution: 2 deg equal-area pixels (~60 km); sensor footprint ~45 km FWHM at 30 km altitude
sources.citation: Prettyman T.H. et al. (2006) JGR 111, E12007.
sources.limitations: Low spatial resolution; values are footprint-averaged; oxides constrained to sum with model assumptions.

sources.name: Lunar Prospector epithermal / thermal / fast neutron counting rates
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Lunar Prospector reduced special products)
sources.citation: Feldman W.C. et al. (2001) JGR 106, 23231; Maurice S. et al. (2004) JGR 109, E07S04.
sources.limitations: Count rates are an INDIRECT hydrogen proxy (lower epithermal = more H); also sensitive to composition; not converted to WEH here.

sources.name: GRAIL GRGM900C Bouguer anomaly and free-air anomaly error maps (l<=600)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (GRAIL)
sources.citation: Lemoine F.G. et al. (2014) GRL 41, 3382; Zuber M.T. et al. (2013) Science 339, 668.
sources.limitations: Bouguer anomalies reflect density contrasts at many depths; NOT direct evidence of voids/caves.

sources.name: Robbins (2018) Lunar Crater Database
sources.provider: USGS Astrogeology (Astropedia)
sources.citation: Robbins S.J. (2019) JGR Planets 124, 871-892.
sources.limitations: Manual catalog; completeness varies with illumination/data; no degradation state.

sources.name: Unified Geologic Map of the Moon, 1:5M (2020)
sources.provider: USGS Astrogeology
sources.citation: Fortezzo C.M. et al. (2020) USGS Unified Geologic Map of the Moon, 1:5M.
sources.limitations: Interpretive map compiled from six regional maps; unit boundaries generalized.

sources.name: LROC Lunar Pit Locations (Lunar Pit Atlas)
sources.provider: LROC Science Operations Center / NASA PDS (LRO-L-LROC-5-RDR-V1.0 extras)
sources.citation: Wagner R.V. & Robinson M.S. (2021) Lunar Pit Atlas; Robinson M.S. et al. (2012) PSS 69, 18.
sources.limitations: Pits are skylight candidates; subsurface extent unknown for nearly all.

sources.name: PGDA polar average solar visibility (illumination) maps
sources.provider: NASA GSFC Planetary Geodesy Data Archive (product 69)
sources.citation: Mazarico E. et al. (2011) Icarus 211, 1066.
sources.limitations: Computed from LOLA topography (ray-casting), not observed; local horizons < 240 m unresolved.

sources.name: Analytic orbital-geometry model (insolation, Earth visibility, liquid-water impossibility)
sources.provider: TerraTwin derivation from standard celestial mechanics
sources.citation: Standard insolation formula (e.g., Berger 1978); lunar optical libration amplitudes 7.9 deg / 6.7 deg.
sources.limitations: Bare-sphere horizon (no topographic shadowing - use PGDA illumination near poles); S0 = 1361 W/m2.

limitations: No conventional wind or aeolian processes exist on the Moon; no wind variables are included (not 'zero', absent).
No lunar biology / biosignature dataset exists; habitability features are physical proxies only.
Water/ice indicators are indirect (neutron count rates, thermal-model ice stability); no direct global ice map.
Polar illumination (PGDA) covers only poleward of 65 deg; elsewhere insolation is an analytic bare-sphere model.
Diviner rock abundance / regolith anomaly cover 60S-60N only.
GRAIL Bouguer residuals are density-anomaly indicators, not evidence of caves or voids.
Pit catalog lists skylight candidates; subsurface extent of nearly all pits is unknown.
Lunar Prospector GRS/neutron data have ~60 km resolution; finer cells inherit the containing bin value.
No global high-resolution geotechnical (bearing strength) map exists.

mars.title: TerraTwin mars integrated dataset

grid.cell_id: row * n_lon + col, row 0 = northernmost, col 0 = -180 E

sources.name: MGS MOLA Mission Experiment Gridded Data Record, 128 px/deg topography
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (MOLA team)
sources.citation: Smith D.E. et al. (2001) JGR 106, 23689; Smith D.E. et al. (2003) MGS-M-MOLA-5-MEGDR-L3-V1.0, NASA PDS.
sources.limitations: Interpolated between MOLA tracks at low latitudes; 88-90 deg excluded at this resolution.

sources.name: Robbins & Hynek Mars crater database (2020 release, D>=1 km, full morphology)
sources.provider: Author distribution (S.J. Robbins) of the peer-reviewed database
sources.citation: Robbins S.J. & Hynek B.M. (2012) JGR 117, E05004.
sources.limitations: The USGS pygeoapi mirror carries only id/lat/lon/diameter, so the author's full release is used; not an official NASA archive.

sources.name: Geologic Map of Mars, USGS SIM 3292 (global geology shapefile)
sources.provider: USGS Publications Warehouse (SIM 3292 database). The USGS pygeoapi mirror returned HTTP 502 for every page on 2026-11-01, so only the geology shapefile members are read from the official database zip via HTTP Range.
sources.citation: Tanaka K.L. et al. (2014) USGS SIM 3292.
sources.limitations: Global-scale generalization; unit age is encoded in the unit code prefix (e/m/l + N/H/A).

sources.name: TES global mineral abundance maps (Bandfield 2002)
sources.provider: ASU Mars Space Flight Facility (TES instrument team) - JMARS WMS numeric layers
sources.citation: Bandfield J.L. (2002) JGR 107, 5042.
sources.limitations: Linear-deconvolution abundances; detection limit ~10-15%; high-albedo dusty regions not retrieved.

sources.name: TES thermal inertia, Lambert albedo, rock abundance and fine-component thermal inertia
sources.provider: ASU Mars Space Flight Facility (TES team) - JMARS WMS numeric layers
sources.citation: Christensen P.R. et al. (2001) JGR 106, 23823; Nowicki S.A. & Christensen P.R. (2007) JGR 112, E05007.
sources.limitations: Thermal inertia from single-layer homogeneous model; rock abundance from multi-wavelength fit (Nowicki & Christensen 2007).

sources.name: OMEGA global spectral parameter maps (ferric, pyroxene, olivine, albedo)
sources.provider: IAS / ESA Mars Express OMEGA team products served by ASU JMARS WMS
sources.native_resolution: 32 px/deg product, retrieved at 8 px/deg through WMS
sources.citation: Ody A. et al. (2012) JGR 117, E00J14.
sources.limitations: Spectral parameters are relative indicators, not abundances; WMS resampling method undocumented.

sources.name: Mars Odyssey GRS elemental and water-equivalent hydrogen maps (5x5 deg smoothed)
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Odyssey GRS team)
sources.citation: Boynton W.V. et al. (2007) JGR 112, E12S99.
sources.limitations: Footprint ~450 km; abundances normalised per GRS team conventions.

sources.name: Mars Odyssey Neutron Spectrometer epithermal neutron map
sources.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node (Odyssey GRS special products)
sources.citation: Feldman W.C. et al. (2004) JGR 109, E09006.
sources.limitations: Indirect hydrogen proxy; seasonal CO2 frost affects polar rates.

sources.name: SWIM ice-consistency maps (Subsurface Water Ice Mapping) via JMARS WMS
sources.provider: SWIM project (PSI / JPL / NASA) served by ASU JMARS WMS (swim.psi.edu returned HTTP 522 on 2026-11-01)
sources.native_resolution: product-dependent (~1-4 km mosaics); retrieved at 0.25 deg
sources.citation: Morgan G.A. et al. (2021) Nature Astronomy 5, 230.
sources.limitations: Consistency score combining neutron, thermal, radar and geomorphic evidence; not an ice detection.

sources.name: Mars Global Cave Candidate Catalog (MGC3)
sources.provider: USGS Astrogeology
sources.citation: Cushing G.E. (2017) Mars Global Cave Candidate Catalog, NASA PDS.
sources.limitations: Candidates only; cave extent not confirmed.

sources.name: Mars Global Digital Dune Database (MGD3)
sources.provider: USGS Open-File Reports 2007-1158 (equatorial polygons) and 2018-1164 (dune composition/TI tables)
sources.citation: Hayward R.K. et al. (2007, 2014); Fenton L.K. et al. (2018) USGS OFR 2018-1164.
sources.limitations: Dune fields >1 km2; small bedforms excluded; polar dune fields (>65 deg) not included in this pipeline.

sources.name: Mars Climate Database v6.2 climatology (web-interface extraction)
sources.provider: LMD / CNES / ESA Mars Climate Database v6.2 public web interface
sources.citation: Millour E. et al. (2018) MCD v6, EPSC; Forget F. et al. (1999) JGR 104, 24155.
sources.limitations: General-circulation-model climatology, NOT observations; coarse GCM grid; local topographic effects absent.

sources.name: Analytic orbital-geometry model (top-of-atmosphere insolation)
sources.provider: TerraTwin derivation from standard celestial mechanics
sources.citation: Allison M. & McEwen M. (2000) PSS 48, 215 (Mars orbital elements).
sources.limitations: Top-of-atmosphere only; MCD insolation_surface_wm2 includes dust attenuation.

limitations: Surface temperature, pressure, wind, dust and insolation are Mars Climate Database MODEL climatology, not observations.
No global biosignature dataset exists; biosignature-preservation features are context proxies only.
MOCAAS hydrated-mineral rasters were unavailable (HTTP 410 at the official URL); aqueous-mineral context relies on TES/GRS proxies.
SWIM ice consistency is a model-based consistency score and covers only the SWIM study region.
Odyssey GRS maps have ~450-600 km footprints (5 deg bins); finer cells inherit the containing bin value.
Cave candidates (MGC3) are surface openings; cave interiors are unmapped.
MOLA 128 ppd topography stops at +-88 deg latitude; dune polygons cover 65S-65N only.
Mars gravity / subsurface radar products were not integrated in this release.
No global high-resolution geotechnical (bearing strength) map exists.
